sections.html:
Garner owners generally pick between a market listing, a private sale and a cash offer, and the shape of the house plus the date you must close usually decide it. Garner borders downtown Raleigh in Wake County, so commuters heading into the city are a steady share of buyers.

  • Market listing: suits a house in good order when you can wait out showings.
  • Private sale: suits owners who can handle contracts and buyer screening alone.
  • Cash offer: fits a house with repairs, a tenant, an inheritance or a payment problem attached.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Garner houses as they stand, so you can set that figure beside the net from a listing after repairs and costs.

Garner is a town of over 45,000 residents beside downtown Raleigh. It runs its own police, fire, public works, inspections and parks departments. Public schools come from the Wake County Public School System, and some of them keep a year-round or modified calendar, which matters to families choosing a move date. Check a Garner address's school assignment with the school system before you advertise it.

sections.h2: How Wake County values a Garner house
sections.html:
Wake County Tax Administration, not the town, sets the value of every Garner parcel. Current values reflect a revaluation effective January 1, 2024, and the next one is effective January 1, 2027.

The commissioners have chosen a two-year cycle after that, starting with January 1, 2029. A revaluation changes assessed values only. A bill is the value multiplied by the rate that elected officials adopt.

In a revaluation year officials must publish a revenue-neutral rate for comparison without having to adopt it. Every owner may appeal a new value to the county's Board of Equalization and Review, and the county publishes a table of home sales that you can search for comparable houses.

sections.h2: Falling behind on a Garner mortgage
sections.html:
A lender usually forecloses by power of sale, with a hearing before the court clerk. G.S. 45-21.16 sets the notice at 10 days before the hearing, and G.S. 45-21.27 lets bidders top a sale price with an upset bid of at least 5 percent and not less than $750.00 more.

A sale that pays off the loan before the foreclosure sale can stop the case. Call a housing counselor or an attorney early, and get any offer in writing.

Garner asks owners of boarded-up residential buildings to file an application with a plan to repair, replace or demolish the structure. The aim is to limit the harm these houses cause nearby.

Residents report substandard housing, tall grass or abandoned cars through the town's info system or by email to the Code Compliance team. If you own a vacant Garner house, a mowed lot and a filed plan help keep a sale moving.

sections.h2: Circuit breaker for owners 65 and older
sections.html:
Qualifying owners can cap their tax at a share of income under G.S. 105-277.1B, and the state form prints the 2026 income figures as $38,800 and $58,200.

Deferred tax under the program is a lien and comes due on a transfer, so a sale triggers it. Ask the Wake County assessor what amount you would owe at closing.

sections.h2: What to line up before listing
sections.html:
Pull together the paperwork and the permits first, because a clean file keeps a Garner sale on schedule. The town's pages point to a permit and inspection portal, a development activity map and a unified development ordinance, and each can answer a question a buyer will ask.

  • Check the portal for permits on past work such as a deck, a roof or an addition.
  • Look at the development map to see what is planned or under construction near your street.
  • Ask the school system which schools are assigned to your address and on what calendar.
  • Collect receipts, warranties and any homeowners association papers.

The town also has a comprehensive plan called Garner Forward and a housing resources page, which show where it expects to grow. Buyers who commute into Raleigh may ask about roads and nearby projects, so know your answers before the first showing.

Property tax for the year is billed to whoever holds title that year, so ask your closing attorney how the bill will be split. The county register of deeds records the deed after closing, and under G.S. 47-18 the buyer is protected against later claims from the time of registration.

sections.h2: How long a Garner sale takes
sections.html:
Timelines vary by route, so ask each buyer to commit to a closing date in writing. A listing runs through photos, showings, offers, the buyer's inspection and a lender's appraisal, and a snag at any step can add weeks. A cash buyer can often cut out the lender and the repair talks.

Garner's position next to Raleigh helps a listing draw commuters, yet a house that needs a roof or heating work may sit while buyers price the repairs. In that case owners sometimes compare a repaired listing against an as-is offer, and the comparison turns on how much the repairs cost and how long a vacant house would carry taxes, insurance and utilities.

If a foreclosure date is on the calendar, work backward from it. Any sale has to close, and pay off the lender, before the foreclosure sale to stop it.

sections.h2: Questions to ask a Garner buyer
sections.html:
Short, direct questions keep an offer honest, and a written answer is worth more than a promise. Ask the following of every Garner buyer before you sign.

  • Is the offer for cash, and is proof of funds available?
  • Who selects the closing attorney, and who pays that attorney?
  • Does the price change after the buyer inspects the house?
  • What is the earnest money, and when is it refundable?
  • Can you stay a few days after closing if you need to move out?

Cash Home Buyers answers those questions in writing for Garner houses, and you can use the same list to test any other offer you receive.

sections.h2: What happens at a Garner closing
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, a closing attorney takes over the paper side. The attorney checks the title, confirms what you owe the lender and the county, and prepares a settlement statement. Ask to see it before signing day and read the seller's column line by line.

  • Loan payoff: the lender sends a figure good through a stated date.
  • Property tax: the year's bill follows whoever holds title, so the statement shows how it is split.
  • Deed: after funds clear, the attorney files it with the Wake County register of deeds.

A cash sale usually skips the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiations that follow a buyer's inspection, which leaves title work as the main wait. A sale to a buyer with a loan adds those steps. Either way, bring photo identification and keys, and plan your move-out date before the closing is set.

faqs.a: Yes. Wake County Tax Administration sets values for Garner houses, and the county register of deeds records the deed.

faqs.q: Can a sale stop a Garner foreclosure?
faqs.a: It can, if the price covers the payoff and closes before the foreclosure sale. Get the lender's payoff figure in writing first.

faqs.q: Who handles code complaints in Garner?
faqs.a: The town's Code Compliance team takes reports by email or through its info app and service request system.

faqs.q: Does Garner have its own school system?
faqs.a: No. Garner schools belong to the Wake County Public School System.

faqs.q: Will my taxes change after the 2027 revaluation?
faqs.a: They can. The bill depends on the new value and on the rate chosen by elected officials, so ask Wake County Tax Administration when notices arrive.
